The Energy Savings Scheme (ESS) and the Peak Demand Reduction Scheme (PDRS) require an Accredited Certificate Provider (ACP) to be nominated as the energy saver or capacity holder to create certificates. This template is the nomination form approved by the Scheme Administrator for all ESS methods and for all PDRS methods except Household Annual Demand Response Activity Definition BESS2.
You must not use this form for BESS2 and the Household Annual Demand Response Method, and instead use the BESS2 Nomination Specification to be nominated as the capacity holder.
It must be used to nominate the ACP as the energy saver/capacity holder for an implementation of an activity at a particular site for the ESS and the PDRS.
To use this template, you will need to:
Copy the wording from pages 3 to 4 of this document into your own document, formatting as appropriate and deleting footnotes.
Fill in Sections 2 and 3 of the form.
Request that the original energy saver/capacity holder completes Sections 1, 4 and 5 of the form, including signing and dating the form.
You must fill in the Implementation details at Section 2 in a way that specifically describes the activity. Make sure to:

Include a full description of the activity and the Activity Definition so that the purchaser understands what will be installed. Providing the Activity Definition label only (e.g. D16) will not be sufficient to meet this requirement.
Describe the quantity of equipment installed/removed. It should be unambiguous which products are specified in the form. Examples include:
1 existing pool pump replaced with new pool pump
Lighting products replaced for 3 bedrooms and 1 living room.
1 gas-fired boiler removed, and replaced with air-source heat pump water heater.
You must give a completed copy of the form to the nominator within 7 days of them signing it. This can be a digital copy or a physical photocopy.

The wording in this template may not be appropriate in all circumstances and may need modifying. If you wish to modify this template’s wording, you must submit your proposed wording to the Scheme Administrator for approval by emailing ESS.Compliance@ipart.nsw.gov.au.

The Energy Savings Scheme (ESS) and the Peak Demand Reduction Scheme (PDRS) create certificates from projects that produce energy savings and/or the capacity to reduce demand on our electricity network during peak times. Nomination Specification 
 
 
 
Independent Pricing and Regulatory Tribunal | NSW 
 
Nomination specification – BESS2 only 
Version 2.1 July 2026 
Purpose of this specification 
This specification details how the account holder of the electricity account who will sign the 
demand response contract (the Original Capacity Holder) is to nominate the Accredited 
Certificate Provider (ACP) to be the Capacity Holder (the Nominated Capacity Holder) for the 
BESS2 activity (Onboard a behind the meter battery energy storage system with a Demand 
Response Aggregator). 
To be nominated as the Capacity Holder under BESS2, the ACP and/or the Demand Response 
Aggregator must design its business processes to meet the specifications set out below.  
You must not use the standard Nomination Form Template for BESS2  
If you are conducting other activities under the Peak Demand Reduction Scheme ( PDRS), or any 
activity under the Energy Savings Scheme, you will need to be nominated separately using the 
standard Nomination Form Template.

Nomination Specification Nomination specification – BESS2 only 
 
 
 
 
Independent Pricing and Regulatory Tribunal | NSW Page | 2 
Nomination specifications 
Form of nomination 
The nomination to the Nominated Capacity Holder must be in writing and signed by the Original 
Capacity Holder within 90 days of the Implementation Date. 
The Original Capacity Holder can sign the nomination using any of the following methods: 
• Typing their name into an online text box 
• An electronic signature on a digital contract 
• A wet-ink signature on a paper contract. 
You or the Demand Response Aggregator (DRA) may use an online system or platform to record 
and manage the nomination process. 
Requirement to provide contact details 
You are required to provide the following contact details to the Original Capacity Holder and a 
copy of the nomination within 7 days of them signing the nomination:  
• The ACP and DRAs names and ABN/ACNs 
• The ACP and DRA’s contact numbers and/or email addresses 
• The ACP’s relevant PDRS accreditation number  
• How the consumer can access customer support for the services they are contracting for in 
the demand response contract.  
Nomination requirements 
The below nomination text must be provided to the Original Capacity Holder. It is good practice 
to show them the nomination before signing the contract. 
You may develop a separate nomination that incorporates the nomination text or incorporate the 
nomination text within the demand response contract.  
The nomination must be displayed with the same prominence as other important information in 
the demand response contract. It must not be in a font size that is smaller than other key terms 
and conditions.  
The Original Capacity Holder must not be asked to sign without reading or be subject ed to high-
pressure sales tactics to sign the demand response contract or nomination.  
The Original Capacity Holder must agree to the nomination text. This can be by agreeing to  the 
contract where the nomination is a condition of the contract, or by separately agreeing to the 
nomination with a separate signature. You must record the date that the Original Capacity Holder 
agrees to the nomination. You may automate this digitally (for example, through a platform such 
as Docusign) or have the Original Capacity Holder complete the date.

Nomination Specification Nomination specification – BESS2 only 
 
 
 
 
Independent Pricing and Regulatory Tribunal | NSW Page | 3 
The nomination text below must be shown to the Original Capacity Holder unbroken on a single 
page or webpage, before signing the nomination. Sections in yellow are to be populated before 
being presented to the Original Capacity Holder while the blue sections are to be filled in by the 
Original Capacity Holder. Purple sections are drafting instructions that must be followed and then 
removed from the final version. 
 
 The Accredited Certificate Provider (ACP) must be nominated within 
90 days of the Implementation Date 
 
An ACP may only create Peak Reduction Certificates from a BESS2 Implementation if 
the ACP is the Nominated Capacity Holder at the time of certificate creation and was 
nominated within 90 days of the Implementation Date. The ACPs must also be the 
most recent Capacity Holder if more than one nomination is made. For the BESS2 
activity, the Implementation Date is the date the Original Capacity Holder’s battery is 
Onboarded with the Demand Response Aggregator (VPP provider) 
Nomination text 
The Peak Demand Reduction Scheme (PDRS) incentivises projects that create capacity to reduce 
the demand on our electricity network during peak times. Onboarding your battery with a virtual 
power plant (VPP) and allowing it to be coordinated with other batteries in the VPP creates Peak 
Demand Reduction Capacity. The incentive is for making your battery available to provide 
electricity when it is needed during peak times, it is not for the actual dispatch of the electricity 
from your battery. That part is taken care of by the VPP provider.  
As the person agreeing to onboard your battery with a VPP you are the Original Capacity Holder, 
and you have the right to that Peak Demand Reduction Capacity. By signing this nomination you 
are giving [Insert ACP name and ABN] the right to create and sell certificates based on that Peak 
Demand Reduction Capacity. This nomination does not relate to the terms and conditions of your 
demand response contract.  
Before you sign this nomination you should separately understand and consider the terms and 
conditions of the demand response contract you are being asked to sign and whether it is right 
for you.  
[Include this note if the ACP and DRA are separate entities, otherwise delete]  Note – [Insert 
ACP name and ABN] and [Insert DRA name and ABN] are not representatives of the NSW 
Government. 
[Include this note if the ACP and the DRA are the same entity, otherwise delete]  Note – [Insert 
ACP name and ABN] is not a representative of the NSW Government. 
You are not required to make this nomination, nor is the party you are contracting with 
representing the NSW Government.

Nomination Specification Nomination specification – BESS2 only 
 
 
 
 
Independent Pricing and Regulatory Tribunal | NSW Page | 4 
I, the person signing below, nominate [Insert ACP name and ABN] as the Capacity Holder for 
the demand reduction capacity created by onboarding my battery to be a part of the virtual 
power plant operated by [Insert name and ABN of the ACP or DRA who is controlling the 
relevant VPP].  
I declare that: 
I agree to provide information about my battery and onboarding it with the VPP to IPART 
or an Energy Security Safeguard Schemes auditor if requested 
I understand that the ACP is required to provide a completed copy of this declaration for 
my records within 7 days of me signing this form. 
There is no life support equipment at the premises. Life support equipment means any 
of the following: 
An oxygen concentrator 
An intermittent peritoneal dialysis machine 
A kidney dialysis machine 
A CPAP respirator 
Crigler Najjar syndrome phototherapy equipment 
A ventilator for life support 
Any other equipment that a registered medical professional certifies is required for a 
person residing at the premises for life support.  
I understand I can only receive this incentive once and no further incentive s are 
available under the scheme for joining another VPP or rejoining this VPP. 
The information I have provided is accurate and is not misleading by inclusion or 
omission.

the demand on our electricity network during peak times. Onboarding your battery with a virtual 
power plant (VPP) and allowing it to be coordinated with other batteries in the VPP creates Peak

Demand Reduction Capacity. This nomination does not relate to the terms and conditions of your 
demand response contract.
